hero.title: An agent stack for
hero.lede: The published Linux arm64 broker is 24.1 MiB; the gateway is 13.0 MiB. Together they give models a host-like workspace without inherited environment variables, host files, or ambient sockets.
hero.caveat: Published v0.10.0 Linux arm64 archive, 22 Aug 2026. Dekopon is pre-production; the current local deployment treats one Unix UID as a trust domain.

broker.title: Start with the broker YAML.
broker.intro: This trimmed, synthetic configuration gives Alice one way to comment on a pull request. The identity, provider, credential name, destination, methods, call count, bytes, and timeout are all visible before the agent starts.
broker.yaml:
apiVersion: dekopon.dev/brokerd/v1alpha1
brokerPrincipal: local-broker
policyRevision: pr-commenter-2026-08
policiesPath: ./policies.cedar
credentialsPath: ./broker-credentials.yaml
providers:
  - ./gh-provider.wasm

identities:
  - uid: 65532
    principal: chat-gateway
    actor: { type: service, principal: chat-gateway }
    attestor:
      namespaces: [slack.example]
      chatScopes:
        - breadth: transportWide
          kind: slack
          transport: workspace-slack
identityMappings:
  - subject: slack.example.u123
    principal: alice

constraintSets:
  gh.pull-request.comment:
    provider: gh
    effect: external-write
    risk: Medium
    idempotency: conditional
    credential: github-comment-token
    constraints:
      timeoutMs: 15000
      maxOutputBytes: 8192
      http:
        allowedHosts: [api.github.com]
        allowedMethods: [GET, POST]
        maxRequests: 2
        maxRequestBytes: 16384
        maxResponseBytes: 262144
        allowPlaintextLoopback: false

status.title: Write the command. Keep its credential away from it.
status.intro: Providers are ordinary Rust components. They declare what they do and, optionally, the command words agents may type. The broker supplies narrowly constrained I/O without handing the component its token.

provider.body: Implement the public Provider trait, compile for wasm32-unknown-unknown, and inspect the final component before loading it.
points: Describe typed capabilities in a manifest

secrets.label: Broker-held credentials · v0.10.0
secrets.title: The tool works without seeing its token.
secrets.body: The agent calls a normal command. The Wasm guest builds a bounded request. Only the native broker HTTP engine can inject the destination-bound credential.

items.name: prompt
items.description: No provider token in model context

items.name: bash
items.description: No inherited environment or host files

items.name: Wasm guest
items.description: No credential import or ambient socket

items.name: broker
items.description: Loads the 0600 file and injects at the bound host

secrets.note: Destination binding keeps the token out of prompts and guest code. It does not make the remote endpoint trustworthy if that endpoint reflects the value.

authority.title: Alice may leave a comment.
authority.intro: In this synthetic deployment, Slack subject slack.example.u123 maps to principal alice. She may drive pr-commenter through chat-gateway, then request one GitHub comment capability.
authority.decisionBody: The rule matches trusted identity and routing context. It never reads Alice’s message or the provider input.
authority.constraintsTitle: The broker then applies the YAML envelope
authority.denial: Route Alice to release-bot and Cedar denies agent.prompt before any model call: the Agent resource no longer matches.

invariants.title: Text cannot become Alice
invariants.body: The principal comes from the gateway attestation and broker mapping, never the prompt.

invariants.title: Prompt is a separate grant
invariants.body: Permission to drive pr-commenter does not imply permission to use its GitHub capability.

invariants.title: Comment is not merge
invariants.body: Each capability is a distinct Cedar action. Missing actions stay denied.

invariants.title: Policy cannot widen I/O
invariants.body: Cedar can allow the action. It cannot add hosts, methods, calls, time, bytes, or credentials.

execution.kicker: Bash, minus the operating system · v0.10.0 provider words
execution.title: Use the shell training models already have.
execution.intro: State-of-the-art models are rigorously trained on normal shell sessions. Dekopon reuses their command discovery, jq, loops, and exit-code recovery without launching /bin/bash. The v0.10.0 broker path also lets providers contribute checked command words.
execution.script:
issue=$(tickets issue show T-42)
echo "$issue" | jq '{title, owner, state}'

for id in $(tickets issue list --state open | jq -r '.[].id'); do
  tickets issue show "$id" | jq '{id, owner, state}'
done
execution.result: one script · bounded JSON · explicit exit codes

cards.title: The training transfers
cards.body: Variables, loops, pipes, command substitution, jq, and exit codes feel like the shell transcripts frontier models already know.

cards.title: Providers become verbs
cards.body: A provider may declare commandWords: ["tickets"]. Its pure resolver turns argv into one typed capability proposal.

cards.title: A command grants nothing
cards.body: Resolving tickets issue show does not authorize it. The same Cedar decision and broker constraints still run.

cards.title: Every loop has a ceiling
cards.body: Script steps, recursion, output, deadline, model turns, tool calls, provider fuel, memory, and broker I/O are all bounded.

deployment.title: One pod. No public control plane.
deployment.intro: The v0.10.0 arm64 image runs the gateway and broker as separate containers in one single-node pod. They share one owner-only Unix socket; an optional Service exposes only the gateway’s signed WhatsApp webhook.
points: A native broker sidecar becomes ready before the gateway starts
An init container turns Kubernetes projections into real owner-only files
Audit state and optional provider storage use separate retained volumes
Provider and model credentials never enter the image

closing.title: Give the agent commands.
closing.titleAccent: Keep the host out of reach.
closing.body: Start with the broker YAML above, add one provider, and let the model use the shell habits it already has. The credential stays with the broker.
